name: Minimally invasive lateral approach to the tibial shaft
corridor: Proximal window 5 cm long, 1.5–2 cm lateral to the crest distal to the tubercle, and a distal window that retracts tibialis anterior with the deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels, then a submuscular epiperiosteal tunnel

positioning.text: Position so proximal and distal lateral windows and a distractor can be used. In children, mark both physes and respect the tubercle apophysis.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the tibial crest, tubercle, and the crossing of the anterior tibial vessels and deep peroneal nerve on the anterolateral face at about the junction of the third and fourth quarters.

incision.text: Make a proximal cut about 5 cm long starting distal to the tubercle and 1.5–2 cm lateral to the crest, curving slightly posterior. Add a distal cut over the distal third when the plate is long (about more than 25 cm in adults) so the bundle can be seen rather than trapped.

superficial_interval.text: Incise fascia a few millimeters lateral to the crest. Distally, lift tibialis anterior from bone while preserving paratenon.

deep_interval.text: Proximally take tibialis anterior off bone without stripping periosteum (and without injuring the apophysis in children) and retract it laterally. Distally retract the tendon with the deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels laterally. Tunnel between muscle and periosteum with an elevator, tunneler, or the plate, passing under the bundle under direct vision.

layers.text: Skin, fascia off the crest, tibialis anterior, intact periosteum, then a submuscular plate tunnel.

structures_at_risk.text: The deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels in the distal third, periosteum, and in children the physes and tubercle apophysis are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Passing a submuscular plate or percutaneous screws across the distal-third bundle without a viewing window, and closing fascia over a swollen compartment, are the danger zones.

retraction_hazards.text: Lift or retract the distal bundle so the plate passes under it under direct observation, not blindly.

exposure.text: Used for lateral MIPO when medial tissues are injured, including precontoured lateral plates for proximal and mid-tibial fractures. Distal contouring and screw placement are difficult.

limitations.text: The distal third is a poor contouring zone and requires an open window to protect the bundle.

indications.text: Indicated for minimally invasive lateral plating when medial skin is injured.

closure.text: Close skin and subcutaneous tissue. Consider leaving fascia open because postoperative compartment syndrome remains a risk. In children, close skin and fat only.

complications.text: Complications include trapping or piercing the distal-third neurovascular bundle and compartment syndrome.

procedure_applications.condition: A proximal or mid-tibial fracture is bridge-plated laterally because medial skin is injured

questions.question: Where do the anterior tibial vessels and deep peroneal nerve cross the anterolateral tibia?
questions.answer: About at the junction of the third and fourth quarters.

questions.question: How is a distal-third lateral plate passed relative to that bundle?
questions.answer: Under direct vision, with the bundle retracted or lifted so the plate and instruments pass beneath it.

questions.question: Where does the proximal window start?
questions.answer: Distal to the tibial tubercle and 1.5–2 cm lateral to the crest, about 5 cm long, curving slightly posterior.
